---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iOS/macOS. One global toggle mixes urgent assigned-task alerts with marketing; disabling in-app toggle claims to override system settings and permission is requested before any project exists. Quiet hours are ignored.

# Apple HIG: End-to-end behavior and recovery

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Trace the person’s task from entry through completion, cancellation, interruption and recovery. Select the pattern procedure for the actual failure or desired behavior before selecting its controls.
2. Preserve the current work, selection and navigation context across the transitions that matter. Choose interruption or modality according to urgency and task scope, not visual emphasis.
3. For asynchronous or recurring work, separate current progress, eventual result, error recovery and unavailable capability. For audio/video/haptics, specify user control and environmental behavior.
4. Deliver a transition/state specification, a correction to the supplied flow, or ranked findings tied to observed steps. Test alternate exits and resumption, not just the success path.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

# Apple HIG: Map the data domain to the control

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify value type, range, precision, number of choices and whether selection commits immediately. Enter the procedure for fields, pickers, sliders, toggles or other suitable controls.
2. Choose a control according to the person’s input task, available space and precision needs. Preserve valid values, locale conventions and useful defaults without silently changing user input.
3. Specify validation and correction in context, including keyboard/paste and alternative access where relevant. Distinguish unavailable actions from invalid entered data.
4. Deliver a field/control contract or a patch that includes value representation, commit/cancel behavior and concrete invalid/edge-value checks.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

name: apple-hig-managing-notifications
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting notification permission, urgency, Focus behavior, and informational or marketing preferences.
---

# Preserve the person's control over interruption

Read [the notification-management guide](../../references/managing-notifications.md). The workflow is application advice; delivery levels and entitlements are source constraints, not guaranteed delivery.

Inspect event categories, personal impact/timing, consent history, preference UI, platform, and create/review/adapt mode. Distinguish communication from noncommunication and marketing from requested information. Record permission/entitlement evidence; do not infer it from an urgent-looking mockup.

Request consent and respect later silencing/Focus/summary choices. Assign Passive/Active/Time Sensitive/Critical from real urgency rather than business attention goals. Time Sensitive concerns immediate personal impact now/within an hour and remains user-controllable; Critical needs the entitlement and an actual urgent health/safety case. Marketing requires separate explicit content-specific opt-in with accept/decline and must never be Time Sensitive. Provide in-app settings for informational/marketing preferences without pretending they override system settings. Use sender-based supported communication integration when relevant. Watch generally follows companion settings with its documented controls.

Implement authorized category/permission/settings behavior, specify an event/urgency/consent matrix, or review exact overclassification and consent defects. Do not send actual notifications merely to demonstrate a proposed policy without authorization.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a shopping app labels every discount Time Sensitive after a generic permission prompt and offers no marketing opt-out. Decision: sales urgency is not immediate personal impact and permission is not specific marketing consent. After: use appropriate ordinary delivery only after explicit promotional opt-in, with independent preference changes and respect for Focus.

Deliver the artifact, event rationale, interruption level, consent source, and preference routes. Verify denied/revoked permission, Focus, opt-out, nonresponding recipients, and entitlement absence. Fail for marketing breakthrough, implied guaranteed delivery, or inaccessible preference withdrawal. Native Focus/delivery/entitlement execution requires separate evidence.

Load [notifications](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-notifications/SKILL.md) for content/actions or [privacy](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-privacy/SKILL.md) for consent and exposure.

---
name: apple-hig-settings
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting app-wide configuration, task-local options, system preferences, and settings access or persistence.
---

# Put an option where its effect is understood

Read [the settings guide](../../references/settings.md). This workflow is application advice; platform locations and system preference scope constrain the design.

Inspect option inventory/frequency, affected scope, defaults, system counterparts, platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Classify task-local, document-wide, app-wide, and system-wide choices. Record actual capability detection/persistence rather than treating a displayed toggle as proof.

Choose sensible defaults and detect capabilities instead of asking for information already known. Keep frequent view/task options beside their visible effect and rare app-wide choices in settings. Do not duplicate system accessibility/authentication/scrolling preferences with misleading scope. Reserve system Settings entries for rare changes. On Mac place app Settings in the app menu with expected access, document setup in File, and use stable settings-pane navigation/title/restoration rather than a customizable main toolbar. Watch cannot add custom entries to system Settings; keep only essential in-app options. Preserve familiar game access where appropriate.

Implement option placement/persistence or provide a scope/default/location contract; reviews identify exact misplaced or contradictory settings. Do not expand a settings redesign into unauthorized global configuration changes.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a Mac map app puts its layer filter in app Settings and a global Reduce Motion copy in the main toolbar, while document scale changes every map. Decision: frequency and scope are inverted. After: keep layers local, respect system motion preference, and separate document scale from app-wide defaults.

Deliver the artifact, option scope, defaults/detection, access, and restoration policy. Verify default/changed values, reopen/last pane, per-document independence, and capability changes. Fail for misleading global/local scope, duplicated conflicting system preference, or lost expected settings access. Native settings/shortcut behavior requires execution evidence.

Load [the-menu-bar](../../../apple-hig-menus-and-actions/.topics/apple-hig-the-menu-bar/SKILL.md), [toggles](../../../apple-hig-selection-and-input/.topics/apple-hig-toggles/SKILL.md), or [onboarding](../apple-hig-onboarding/SKILL.md) for access, state controls, or deferred setup.

---
name: apple-hig-toggles
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting binary settings, checkboxes, radio choices, mixed state, and stateful buttons.
---

# Expose state rather than disguise an action

Read [the toggle guide](../../references/toggles.md). This procedure is application advice; preserve the source's style and platform distinctions.

Inspect setting meaning, affected content, dependencies, aggregate selection, platform, and create/review/adapt mode. Determine whether the control changes opposing states, executes a command, or selects one value from a list. Record actual state and immediate/deferred persistence; a colored switch does not prove the setting applied.

Use a toggle for state and name its affected content clearly. Differentiate on/off beyond color. On iOS/iPadOS use switches in labelled list rows and appropriate stateful buttons outside; do not add brand color without a reason. On Mac preserve established checkbox patterns, use a prominent switch to enable a group where appropriate, and keep switches/checkboxes/radios in the window body. Reflect mixed aggregate checkbox state when children differ. Use independent checkboxes for multiple choices and radio groups for mutually exclusive choices; larger sets can fit a pop-up. Do not replace a single binary checkbox with an unexplained multi-choice radio model.

Implement the state/dependency binding, provide a state table, or review exact contradictory state and labeling defects. If applying the setting can fail, specify truthful state/recovery according to the product rather than allowing the visual toggle to imply success.

**Worked transformation:** Before: selecting some folders leaves a master “Include All” checkbox checked, and red alone signals disabled sync. Decision: aggregate state and binary meaning are misleading. After: show mixed selection with a dash, allow explicit all/none behavior, and use distinct state shape/fill plus clear sync status.

Deliver the artifact, state meanings, dependencies, aggregate behavior, and persistence contract. Verify both directions, mixed children, unavailable dependencies, and noncolor interpretation. Fail for state displayed opposite to applied behavior, independent options made exclusive, or no way to perceive mixed/off state. Report native value announcement/input separately.

Use [pop-up-buttons](../../../apple-hig-menus-and-actions/.topics/apple-hig-pop-up-buttons/SKILL.md) for larger exclusive sets or [buttons](../../../apple-hig-menus-and-actions/.topics/apple-hig-buttons/SKILL.md) for commands.

---
name: apple-hig-privacy
description: Use when designing or reviewing permission timing, purpose strings, pre-permission explanations, tracking requests, data minimization, or private platform inputs.
---

# Ask for precise access when its purpose is clear

Read [Privacy](../../references/privacy.md). Inspect the feature's actual data needs, transfers, storage, current permission flow, and supported platform. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Produce the requested copy/flow/data-handling changes in the existing stack; distinguish documented platform restrictions from additional application recommendations.

Map each requested category to a specific feature and minimum necessary scope. Remove collection without a concrete benefit; prefer on-device work where it avoids unnecessary transfer. Explain collection/use accurately and flag App Store disclosure updates needed when behavior changes. Respect private email and tracking choices rather than designing around them.

Ask when the person invokes the feature. Launch-time requests need an essential, obvious dependency. Write a short active purpose sentence explaining use and reason. If context is sufficient, omit a custom pre-alert; if explanation is essential, use one clear continuation to the real system alert without imitating Allow/Don't Allow. Keep the guide's special pre-alert restrictions distinct from ordinary onboarding. Tracking requires its system authorization before collection and must not be incentivized or manipulated.

Choose one-time location access for suitable individual tasks using the system location button on supported platforms; preserve permitted customization and all localized/accessibility-sized text. Protect secrets with established authentication/keychain mechanisms. For Mac, account for sandboxing/distribution and fast user switching. For visionOS, separate system rendering assistance from permission-gated Full Space ARKit data; gaze remains private, and imported phone-camera assumptions may need removal or content import.

**Before → decision → after:** A bird journal asks for contacts, microphone, and continuous location at launch although only “Attach current location” uses location. Decision: request only the specific action's needed access. After, journaling works immediately; the attachment action offers the supported location control, and its purpose explains adding the sighting's location.

Deliver a data-purpose/access matrix and corrected permission sequence/copy or implementation. Fail if collection precedes required consent, copy obscures the real use, or unrelated work is gated on optional access. Report code/flow evidence separately from actual authorization prompts and privacy-setting behavior; this procedure does not certify security or legal compliance.

Use [Sign in with Apple](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-sign-in-with-apple/SKILL.md) for that authentication choice and [Augmented reality](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-augmented-reality/SKILL.md) when room/camera access is essential.

# Managing notifications Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-notifications) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Request permission before sending notifications and respect later system choices, including silencing. Some locales exempt government alerts from complete silencing. Notifications can remain available even while Focus delays their alerts. ## Integrating with Focus Focus filters interruption by activity and allowed contacts/apps; scheduled summaries defer alerts to selected times. Communication notifications use sender-based decisions through supported SiriKit intents. Assign an interruption level to other notifications: | Level | Intended urgency | Scheduled delivery override | Focus breakthrough | Silent override | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Passive | Leisurely information | No | No | No | | Active | Ordinary timely update; default | No | No | No | | Time Sensitive | Direct immediate personal impact | Yes | Yes | No | | Critical | Urgent health/safety need | Yes | Yes | Yes | Critical requires an entitlement because it can override delivery, Focus, and silent settings. People can choose whether Time Sensitive alerts break through. ## Best practices Assign urgency honestly to preserve trust. Time Sensitive belongs to events happening now or within an hour, not merely content the app wants noticed. The system introduces and periodically re-evaluates this permission with the person, who can turn it off. ## Sending marketing notifications Send promotions only after an explicit opt-in describing the content with a clear accept/decline choice. Never classify marketing as Time Sensitive. Provide an in-app notification settings screen so people can change informational and marketing preferences. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### watchOS Watch generally inherits the companion iPhone's notification settings. People can change them in the iPhone Watch app or through per-notification actions after a left swipe, such as temporary mute or disabling Time Sensitive alerts. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Privacy](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) #### Developer documentation #### Videos

# Settings Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Use sensible defaults and respect system preferences. App-wide configuration, task-local controls, and system Settings belong in different places according to how often and where people need them. ## Best practices Optimize defaults for most people and automatically detect capabilities such as connected controllers or appearance. Keep the settings set small. Support expected access, including Command-Comma and game Escape. Do not duplicate systemwide accessibility, scrolling, or authentication settings in a way that suggests they have different scope. ## General settings Put infrequently changed experience-wide choices, such as window configuration, saving behavior, key mappings, or account preferences, in the app's settings area. ## Task-specific options Expose frequent view/task changes where their effects are visible: filtering, reordering, and showing/hiding content. In games, approach to a current challenge normally belongs to gameplay rather than a settings trip. ## System settings Reserve system-app entries for the rarest changes and, where useful, link directly from the app. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### macOS Place Settings in the app menu, not the main toolbar; document-level configuration belongs in File. A settings window can use a stable noncustomizable always-visible pane toolbar with active selection. Dim minimize/zoom because reopening is easy and size follows the pane. Use the current pane as title, or App Name Settings for one pane, and restore the previously visited pane. ### watchOS Apps do not add custom entries to system Settings. Offer only essential options, perhaps at the main view's bottom or through More for object configuration. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Onboarding](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — Foundation ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 10, 2024.

# Toggles Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toggles) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A toggle controls opposing states, commonly on/off. The system offers styles such as switches and checkboxes, while buttons can also retain toggle state through appearance changes. ## Best practices Use toggles for state, and another component for actions or selection from a list. Identify the affected content through context or an appropriate label. Toggle buttons typically use a meaningful glyph plus a changed background. Make state differences clear through shape, fill, checkmark, or dot; color alone is insufficient. ## Platform considerations No extra tvOS, visionOS, or watchOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS Use switch-style toggles in list rows where row content supplies the label. Keep the normal green unless a different accent is necessary, and ensure the on appearance contrasts with off. Outside lists, use a stateful button. A familiar icon and obvious state appearance should explain the visible button without an added explanatory label. ### macOS Place switches, checkboxes, and radio buttons in the window body rather than the toolbar or status bar. #### Switches A switch has stronger visual emphasis than a checkbox; use it for prominent settings or enabling an entire settings group. In grouped forms, a mini switch fits the height of a single row. A regular primary switch plus mini subordinate switches can express hierarchy. Retain established checkboxes rather than replacing them merely for a new appearance. #### Checkboxes Checkboxes show empty/off, checkmark/on, or dash/mixed states, usually with a trailing title; editable checklists can omit the title. Leading alignment and indentation make checkboxes useful for hierarchical dependencies. A group label can clarify related choices; align its baseline with the first checkbox. Reflect aggregate mixed state when subordinate choices differ. Use radio buttons when more than two choices must be mutually exclusive. #### Radio buttons Radio groups commonly contain 2–5 labeled circles and allow one choice. A mixed state is possible but rarely useful; a checkbox usually communicates mixed state better. Use checkboxes for multiple independent choices or a lone binary setting. A pair of explicit radio labels can help only when a single checkbox cannot explain the opposing meanings. For more than about 5 options, evaluate a pop-up. When arranged horizontally, allocate consistent space based on the longest label. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: March 29, 2024, September 12, 2023.

# Privacy Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Keep App Store privacy disclosures accurate for new releases and updates; people rely on them before downloading. ## Best practices Collect only what the specific feature requires and make access as precise as possible. Respect Hide My Email, Mail Privacy Protection, and tracking choices. Prefer on-device processing, including Create ML/Neural Engine where useful, to avoid unnecessary server transfers. Use system encryption, key management, and established security protections, including CloudKit’s additional encrypted data types where available. ## Requesting permission Protected categories include personal/location/health/financial/contact information, user-created content, messages/calendar/music/gameplay/HomeKit data, media, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/local network resources, camera/microphone, the advertising identifier, and permission-gated ARKit data in a visionOS Full Space. The system displays the app’s purpose string and stores choices/descriptions in privacy settings. Ask when the person invokes the relevant feature. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. Write a short, specific, active, complete sentence in sentence case with a period, explaining both use and reason. Vague promises of a better experience and commands to enable access do not explain the need. ### Pre-alert screens, windows, or views Usually context explains the request. If extra explanation is essential, use one button clearly leading to the system alert, such as Continue/Next; do not label it Allow or mimic the actual consent choice. Do not add cancellation, close, or other actions except those needed for legal consent. These restrictions apply to pre-permission custom explanations, not ordinary unrelated onboarding screens. ### Tracking requests Show the AppTrackingTransparency alert before collecting tracking information, including if tracking begins at launch. Do not offer incentives, imitate a permission prompt, display an image of the alert, annotate behind it, or otherwise manipulate rushed choices. Such patterns can cause App Review rejection. A legally required consent view before/after the system alert is permitted by the source’s stated review guidance. ## Location button On iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, the system location button provides one-time access at the task’s moment of need. The first tap teaches and confirms its behavior through a system alert; later taps grant access without repeating that education. Authorization expires when app use ends. With no prior status it resembles Allow Once; an existing While Using status is unchanged. Use it for individual tasks such as attaching a location or finding a nearby item/store. Customize only the supplied title, filled/outline glyph, foreground/background colors, and corner radius. Keep all localized and accessibility-size text untruncated and maintain contrast/transparency limits. Persistent customization violations can prevent location access even though the button still triggers other app actions. ## Protecting data Prefer passkeys; if passwords remain, add two-factor verification. Use Face ID, Optic ID, or Touch ID to protect continued signed-in access where appropriate. Store secrets in the encrypted keychain, never plaintext files even with restrictive permissions. Prefer established authentication, Sign in with Apple, and Password AutoFill over invented schemes. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### macOS Sign externally distributed apps with a valid Developer ID. Use sandboxing to limit resource/data access; Mac App Store apps require it. Account for fast user switching rather than assuming the current person is the only signed-in account. ### visionOS System ARKit algorithms support lighting, mapping, persistence, segmentation, and related rendering in Shared Space without exposing raw data to apps. ARKit API access requires Full Space, and plane estimation, scene reconstruction, image anchoring, and hand tracking require permission. Gaze remains private: system hover feedback can respond before a tap without disclosing where someone looks. Compatibility back-camera input is blank; front-camera input represents spatial Personas with permission. Adapt imported phone/tablet camera-dependent features by removal or content import instead of assuming conventional camera capture. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 21, 2023.

item.text: The brief identifies four issues: bundled marketing consent, misleading claims about system settings, premature permission requests, and ignored quiet hours. I’ll separate notification categories, keep system authorization distinct from app preferences, and make quiet hours apply to every category—including urgent task alerts.

# Match the choice structure to its scale

Read [the picker guide](../../references/pickers.md). This workflow is application advice; consult the source for supported date styles/modes rather than assuming every combination works.

Inspect the option count/order, value constraints, locale/calendar/time zone needs, platform/input, and create/review/adapt mode. Establish whether the task is selecting an instant, date, duration, or ordinary option. Record stored semantics separately from displayed formatting.

Use a picker for medium/long ordered lists, simpler controls for short sets, and searchable/indexed layouts for very large datasets. Put it near the edited value and arrange hidden choices predictably. For minute intervals choose a divisor of 60. On iOS/iPadOS select a supported date style/mode combination: countdown cannot use inline/compact and has a bounded duration. Let locale determine order instead of hardcoding month/day assumptions. On Mac choose textual precision versus graphical calendar browsing. On watch choose Crown-friendly wheels or navigation-link lists. Do not invent unsupported API behavior in the user's stack.

Implement the value/display/commit behavior, supply a concrete choice/date specification, or review exact constraint and locale failures. Define invalid/out-of-range incoming values without silently changing the person's meaning.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a scheduling form hardcodes month/day/year, uses 7-minute wheel steps, and offers a compact countdown. Decision: order must localize, minute steps must divide 60, and the chosen mode/style is unsupported. After: use locale ordering, a suitable interval such as 5 minutes, and an allowed duration presentation.

Deliver the artifact, ordered choices, stored semantics, bounds, and commit policy. Verify locale/calendar changes, boundary values, keyboard entry where supported, and edits/cancellation. Fail for a wrong date meaning, unreachable valid option, unsupported mode/style, or silent constraint violation. Separate logic checks from native calendar/Crown/keyboard execution.

Use [pop-up-buttons](../../../apple-hig-menus-and-actions/.topics/apple-hig-pop-up-buttons/SKILL.md) for compact single choice or [lists-and-tables](../../../apple-hig-layout-and-organization/.topics/apple-hig-lists-and-tables/SKILL.md) for very large sets.

# Pickers Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pickers) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Pickers offer scrollable, ordered choices for single or multipart values. Language and locale affect displayed values and order. Date pickers can also use calendars and numeric entry. ## Best practices Use a picker for a medium or longer list. A short list may work better in a pull-down; a very large dataset may need a resizable list or indexed table. Arrange values logically so hidden choices are predictable, for example alphabetically. Present the picker near the edited field, commonly at the bottom of the window or in a popover, instead of forcing a separate navigation step. Minute wheels default to 0–59. A coarser interval is allowed if it divides 60 evenly; 15-minute steps produce 0, 15, 30, and 45. ## Platform considerations visionOS has no additional rules in this source. ### iOS, iPadOS Date entry supports touch, hardware keyboards, and pointers. Choose among these styles: | Style | Presentation | | --- | --- | | Compact | Current value in an accent-colored button; activation opens a modal calendar/time editor | | Inline | Calendar for dates and dates with time; a time-only button reveals wheels | | Wheels | Scrolling value wheels with built-in or hardware keyboard entry | | Automatic | The system chooses for the platform and mode | Modes are date (month/day/year), time (hour/minute and optional AM/PM), date with time, and countdown (hours/minutes, maximum 23 hours 59 minutes). Countdown is unavailable with inline and compact styles. The exact ordering follows device location. Compact is useful for tight space and permits multiple date/time edits before tapping outside to confirm. ### macOS A textual picker saves space and supports precise entry. A graphical picker suits calendar browsing, date-range selection, or a clock-face presentation. ### tvOS SwiftUI Picker provides picker support. ### watchOS The Digital Crown enables precise movement through choices. Wheel styles support ordinary values and dates/times; configure outlines, captions, and scroll indicators as needed. For longer lists, a navigation-link picker displays a button that opens the list, and also allows crown scrubbing without opening it. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Pull-down buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pull-down-buttons) [Lists and tables](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lists-and-tables) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 5, 2023.

# Notification preferences: revised interaction specification

## Scope and decisions

For the iOS/macOS shared project app described in `interface.md`. This is a framework-agnostic design contract, not an SDK implementation. Preferences belong to the signed-in person; changing them never changes teammates’ preferences or project activity history.

The supplied interface bundles urgent assigned-task alerts with marketing, requests permission before a project exists, claims an app toggle overrides system settings, and ignores quiet hours. Replace that global toggle with independent content choices, contextual authorization, and an explicit delivery policy.

HIG-backed decisions:

- Separate informational preferences from marketing. Marketing requires explicit, content-specific acceptance and an equally clear decline; system authorization is not marketing consent. Never use Time Sensitive for marketing. [Managing notifications — Sending marketing notifications](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-notifications#Sending-marketing-notifications)
- Respect system authorization, Focus, scheduled summaries, and later silencing. App preferences control what the app submits; they cannot grant authorization or guarantee presentation. [Managing notifications — Integrating with Focus](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-notifications#Integrating-with-Focus)
- Ask for permission when the person invokes notification functionality, after its purpose is clear. Project creation and ordinary work remain available after refusal. [Privacy — Requesting permission](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Requesting-permission)
- Keep personal app-wide preferences in app Settings; expose a route from project context to the same preferences. On macOS support App menu → Settings and Command-Comma, and restore the last settings pane. [Settings](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings)
- Use labeled switch rows on iOS and independent labeled checkboxes in the macOS settings body. Show state through position/checkmarks as well as color. Permission requests are commands, not switches. [Toggles](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toggles)

Product decisions, rather than Apple requirements: quiet hours apply even to urgent tasks; no breakthrough option is provided; new-user task preferences default on, marketing defaults off; all task alerts initially use Active. No Critical entitlement or validated Time Sensitive use case is supplied.
